rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Every pronoun/demonstrative traced to an in-chunk or earlier-chunk named antecedent. Closest-to-violating: chunk 5 line 60 "Amp changed its mind about the whole mechanism" — 'the whole mechanism' resolves to Handoff/compaction named two sentences earlier in the same chunk (line 58). No forward or never-named referent found.

No chunk points at another file by position. External links are named by title/claim (e.g. chunk 2's plugin link, chunk 8's 'Dino's skill stacking system' link at line 131). The only cross-file pointer ('Pairs with lectures/composing-the-workflow.md') is in the maintainer meta at line 149, below the maintainer cut and exempt from body scope.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -niE "you (did|saw|caught|ran|wrote|built|opened|used)" over body (lines 1-144) → 0 matches. This is a progressive reading page with no session-tied 'the X you did' construction anywhere in the body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -niE "guess|predict" over body (lines 1-144) → 0 matches. No guess-before-reveal beat exists in this file; it is a reading walk, not a demo.

Every chunk (1-9) carries a self-sufficient claim or paragraph on its own topic; none is a bare wait-state or single context-dependent bullet. Closest-to-thin: chunk 1 (lines 5-13) is only 3 short numbered rules, but each is a complete, self-carrying statement, not a fragment.

Every header names exactly what its chunk delivers, e.g. chunk 5 header 'Feedback-loopable methodology and shipped primitives, Sourcegraph Amp' (line 52) accurately previews the two named artefacts (Feedback Loopable, Handoff) the chunk covers; chunk 9 'How to pick what to study' (line 133) previews the three filters that follow. No header contradicted by its own content.

No 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction found. Enumerations like chunk 3 line 30 'There is no compose skill, no orchestrator, no master entry point' and chunk 7 line 93 'No marketplace, no Git-checked-in kit, no orchestrator' are single-sentence factual lists, not the banned two-sentence-then-declarative tic. No anaphora/epistrophe triples found. Line 79 'The single tip Cherny names as most important' attributes the superlative to Cherny's own words, not a self-grading claim about this training's content — grep -niE 'one of the (most|best)|most (important|useful|valuable)' over body → only this one hit, and it is attributive, not value-prop leak. No number+retraction pattern, no abstraction-noun stacks, no empty-leg verb triplets found.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 5 "Feedback-loopable methodology and shipped primitives, Sourcegraph Amp": line 54: "Two artefacts in the Amp surface, with different bylines and different shapes." and line 60: "What's distinctive about the Amp surface: composition seams ship inside Amp's runtime..." — chunk 9 "How to pick what to study": line 137: "If your team has standardised on Amp's runtime, Metcalf and the Amp surface by default." Harm check: 'surface' as a noun compound ('the Amp surface') is the exact specimen the rule bans ('surface as noun ("writing surface")'), distinct from the cleared verb usage ('surface the issue', also present at line 77 'existing tool surface' — that one is a defensible ordinary compound, not flagged). 'The Amp surface' does not read as plain engineering English the way 'API surface' or 'attack surface' do; it echoes this repo's own internal habit of naming things 'X surface' (writing surface, buyer-facing surface) that recurs pervasively in the maintainer-facing compendiums. An AE101 engineer reading 'the Amp surface' on a projected slide has to guess whether it means Amp's product, its docs, or something else — the ambiguity is the harm §8 exists to prevent.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Swap 'the Amp surface' for 'Amp' or 'the Amp product' in both chunk 5 occurrences and the chunk 9 occurrence.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 1 "What this walk covers (and doesn't)": lines 9, 11, 13 each open a numbered bullet with a FULL SENTENCE bolded (e.g. line 9: "**One published framework lives in this set: Klaassen's Compound Engineering.**" — 10 words, far past the ≲5-word handle cap), all three bullets on one slide — the exact 'every bullet opens with a bolded sentence' monoculture the rule names as the violation shape, not a menu/reading-list (this is a list of reading RULES to internalize, not a scan-for-your-entry-point menu, so the lookup-surface waiver does not apply). chunk 8 "Skill stacking system, Dino: the worked example": lines 115, 116, 117, 121, 122, 123, 124 each bold a bullet lead (**A single orchestrator**, **Phase-organised skill catalogue.**, **Seven design principles**, **Front-loaded read-only analysis.**, **Mandatory gates fire positionally**, **Re-invocation as control flow.**, **CLAUDE.md as half the system.**) plus line 126 **scales cross-repo** — 8 bolded elements on one slide, none of them a §34 task-sizing callout or a What-You'll-Learn LO bullet (the two named exceptions), so the ≤1-per-slide budget is not waived here.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Chunk 1: unbold the sentences, keep at most the practitioner name/term as the bolded handle. Chunk 8: flatten most bullet leads to plain prose; keep bold only for the 1-2 handles the slide most needs (e.g. the single orchestrator name).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Read site/layouts/slides.js buildDeckModel (lines 220-290): when no `.phase--lecture/.phase--exercise` nodes are found, the renderer falls back to walking `:scope > section.module` and slide-ifies phase-less content (prework, supplementary, reference) in place under a kind-labelled divider (line 237-258, kind code 'S' for supplementary per line 205 `id.indexOf('supplementary-') === 0`). This file is a supplementary page and reaches the composed deck via that fallback path, not dropped as the 2026-07-09 incident the rule cites.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering — position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran: node scripts/check-slide-numbering.js 2>&1 | grep -i -B2 -A2 "workflow-composition-lineages" → no output (no violations for this file). Headers are never hand-numbered (topic/name labels only, e.g. '## Compound Engineering, Kieran Klaassen'). Body numbered lists (chunk 1's 1/2/3, chunk 9's 1/2/3) are content ordinals inside a paragraph list, not `## Phase N:` / `## N.` step headers, so they are not the class of ordinal this rule governs, and both lists are self-contained 1-2-3 sequences with no cross-reference to renumber.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide size — 210 words / 6 bullets, and the cap is machine-checked.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran: node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/supplementary/workflow-composition-lineages.md → 'oversized: 7' of 9 measured slides: line 102 chunk 8 Dino [609w, 12 bullets]; line 52 chunk 5 Amp [366w]; line 69 chunk 6 Cherny [336w, 9 bullets]; line 89 chunk 7 Ronacher [277w]; line 15 chunk 2 Klaassen [275w]; line 26 chunk 3 Pocock [216w]; line 133 chunk 9 How-to-pick [212w]. No '**Slide size accepted:** <heading> — <reason>' line for any of these headings exists in the maintainer block (only a Slide deixis accept-note is present, line 147). All 7 are over the 210-word ceiling with no accept-path invoked.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Either trim each oversized chunk toward the 210-word / 6-bullet ceiling (the Dino chunk at 609w/12 bullets is the extreme outlier and the best trim candidate), or add a per-heading 'Slide size accepted' maintainer note for the sections that are deliberately dense reference material.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Rule 15's text names exercise headings (imperative/phase-label) and lecture headings (claims) explicitly and only those two file types ('Exercise ## headings = ...; Lecture headings = ...'). This file is a supplementary progressive-reading page (per curriculum/CLAUDE.md's four student-facing types), not an exercise or lecture, and its headers follow a third convention (practitioner-name/topic labels, e.g. 'Compound Engineering, Kieran Klaassen'). The rule does not extend to that type.
